note: #2303. Answers `street: "Washington"` and locality null. The ZIP places the coordinate correctly, which is why every coordinate-graded instrument reads this as a pass. `123 Main St, Washington, DC 20003` parses the locality correctly, and so does `Washington, DC` with no ZIP — the bare city-plus-ZIP surface is the one no US corpus recipe emits.

#2303, the sharpest instance: the city's second token is a street-type word, so it answers `street: "Sioux"` + `street_suffix: "Falls"`. A city whose name ends in a street type has the strongest pull toward the street reading.
#2303. `street: "Arlington"` + `street_suffix: "Heights"` — the same street-type tail as Sioux Falls, on a different suffix word.

#2303. A two-token city with NO street-type word in it, so the street reading is not the tail — the whole name goes to `street`. Included to keep the family from reading as a street-suffix defect alone.
#2303's CONTROL — the surface passes for some cities, so a fix must not be read off the four failures alone. 54.3% of 604 distinct US cities answer correctly in this shape; this is one of them.
